resolutions.researcher_notes: Value 'operating' supported: egy-map.com (Egypt's Projects Map) lists the line as 'تم تنفيذه' (completed), completion Nov 2019, purpose to feed Beni Suef power station; presidency.eg carries the same project under national projects (URL token الواسط verified). Marked medium/not-independent because egy-map explicitly cites the Presidency site as its data source, so the two share one official origin. Indirect corroboration that the line is in service: the 4,800 MW Beni Suef combined-cycle plant it feeds has been operating since 2019. The old current_ref petro-news.com/95212 returned 200 but no longer contains the pipeline text (dead/repurposed).

Value 65 km confirmed by two independent origins: World Bank ESIA for the EG-Giza North Power Project (P116194) explicitly lists item 3 'El Wasta – Beni Suef gas pipeline (65 km) + gas decompression station (in Beni Suef Power Station)'; egy-map.com independently states length 65 km (also 36-inch diameter). Both verified via url_verifier (tokens 'El Wasta' / '65').

Route El Wasta (الواسطي) → Beni Suef (بني سويف), Beni Suef governorate, Egypt confirmed by two independent origins: World Bank ESIA names 'El Wasta – Beni Suef gas pipeline' terminating at a gas decompression station in Beni Suef Power Station; egy-map.com locates the project in Beni Suef governorate. Consistent with GEM StartLocation=El Wasta / End=Beni Suef. Note: WB doc frames it as the third of nine GASCO feeder lines (Dahshour–El Wasta is the upstream segment).

Value 555,000,000 EGP confirmed: egy-map.com states cost '555 مليون جنيه' (555 million EGP); token '555' verified live. Single official origin — egy-map cites the Presidency website as its source, and the presidency.eg page for the same project (national projects registry) is where the figure originates (its cost digits render in Arabic-Indic form so did not match the ASCII '555' token check). No independent second source for the cost figure found; tier medium.

CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: GEM lists Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS), 100%. No source names EGAS as the direct owner of this line. The World Bank ESIA states the nine feeder pipelines (incl. El Wasta–Beni Suef) 'will be implemented by GASCO' — the Egyptian Company for Natural Gas (GASCO), the state gas-transmission operator that is a subsidiary of EGAS; egy-map attributes the project to the Ministry of Petroleum. So the cited source supports state gas-sector ownership under the EGAS umbrella but names GASCO (the transmission operator/implementer), not EGAS holding directly. Suggest a human check on whether Owner should be refined to GASCO (operator) with EGAS as parent. Tier low given the named-entity mismatch.
